content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 Canary alert 1: high error rate during deploy v2026.03.15-b. Canary /v1/embeddings error rate increased to 24% for canary cohort. Auto-paging oncall.

maya (oncall): ack. paging @rafael and @jess. deploy-bot, what's the rollout state?

deploy-bot: pipeline v2026.03.15-b started 11:05 UTC. Canary ramp to 7% at 11:09. At 11:12 error budget exceeded. Migration task 4901 (enum update for account_tier) triggered as part of release. Status: blocked.

jess (engineer): app logs show: `ERROR: invalid input value for enum account_tier: "premium"` on write path and occasional `ERROR: column "account_tier" does not exist` from a stale service instance. Seems like schema and code are out of sync.

rafael (dbops): looking at migration 4901: it attempts to add new enum value 'premium' to type account_tier and then change some columns to use the new value. The ALTER TYPE is waiting on lock because of an ongoing long-running read from analytics (COPY) that started at 10:58.

analytics-bot: Heads-up  analytics export job #842 started 10:58 UTC (COPY TO). Owner: analytics-team.

rafael (dbops): quick check:
```sql
SELECT pid, usename, state, query, query_start, wait_event
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE datname='redwood_prod' AND state <> 'idle' ORDER BY query_start DESC;
```
Blocker: pid 52700 running COPY TO, started 10:58, holding a SHARE lock that prevents ALTER TYPE needing a stronger lock.

maya (oncall): options: 1) terminate the analytics COPY session to allow migration; 2) pause the canary (flip feature flag) and roll back code; 3) rewrite migration to be additive without requiring lock. What's lowest-customer-impact path?

jess (engineer): safest and fastest is to stop routing canary traffic to the new binary (feature-flag kill), let analytics finish or be re-run, and then perform a non-blocking migration path. If we kill the session we may cause analytics to re-run and impact internal reporting.

olivia (support): customers are reporting 500s for embedding requests. We've triaged ~9 tickets in the last 15m; two customers flagged as high priority. We should send an interim notice.

maya (oncall): flipping feature flag `account_tier_v2_enabled` -> OFF to halt canary traffic.

maya (oncall): :white_check_mark: `account_tier_v2_enabled` toggled OFF. Canary traffic dropped to 0% within ~50s. Observed error rate drop from 24% -> 2.6%.

deploy-bot: Canary stopped; rollout paused.

rafael (dbops): since canary is halted, we will NOT force-terminate analytics session. Plan B: perform a non-destructive migration sequence that doesn't require exclusive lock:
1) ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS account_tier_v2 text DEFAULT NULL;
2) backfill account_tier_v2 = account_tier::text in batched writes;
3) update app to use COALESCE(account_tier_v2, account_tier::text) for business logic;
4) later, if desired, convert to enum and drop legacy path in a maintenance window.

We'll run a dry-run first.

rafael (dbops): dry-run SQL:
```sql
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS account_tier_v2 text;
-- backfill in small batches using primary key range to avoid long transactions
COMMIT;
```

jess (engineer): implementing compatibility change in code: read path will use `COALESCE(account_tier_v2, account_tier::text)` and write path will write to both columns for now. Pushing small canary binary is blocked by feature flag off; we'll keep flag off until backfill completes.

olivia (support): posted initial customer status: "We detected errors for a subset of API requests during a canary deploy. The canary has been paused while engineers apply a safe migration. We're monitoring and will update every 30 minutes." Customers acknowledged receipt.

rafael (dbops): kicking off backfill job with batch size 10k rows, throttle to keep replication lag < 5s. Monitoring script logs progress.

deploy-bot: backfill progress: 0% -> 25% -> 61% -> 100% over 22 minutes. Replica lag stayed within acceptable bounds.

rafael (dbops): verification: `SELECT count(*) FROM customers WHERE account_tier_v2 IS NULL;` -> 0. Also spot-checked sample rows. Good to proceed with app compatibility verification.

jess (engineer): integration tests run against a staging snapshot that includes both columns. Tests pass. Preparing to re-enable feature flag to run a controlled canary: 3% traffic for 10 minutes then ramp to 10% if stable. Rollback criteria: absolute error rate > 1.5% over baseline or any consumer 5xx spike.

maya (oncall): handing monitoring to @jess for the canary re-enable. I'm stepping out in 20m. Please ping if anything changes.

jess (engineer): enabling feature flag `account_tier_v2_enabled` -> ON (canary 3%).

jess (engineer): canary at 3% for 12 minutes, metrics stable. Proceeding to ramp to 10%.

deploy-bot: ramp to 10% complete. Observed error delta 0.1% vs baseline. No new high-severity customer tickets during this window.

olivia (support): updated affected customers with wrap-up note and ETA for final postmortem. They appreciated the fast rollback.

maya (oncall): INCIDENT CLOSED for now 1: canary was paused, safe migration applied, compatibility changes deployed, canary re-enabled successfully. Postmortem required. Action items: enforce DB migration checklist (additive-only for enum-like changes), add pre-deploy check for long-running COPY/export sessions, add runbook for fast feature-flag kill + customer comms template, and require a small integration test that validates schema compatibility on canary.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED  P0 -> closed (postmortem pending). :white_check_mark:
